title: Willie Guitars' bass trap door and the Paul English Players tent show
summary: A funny story about the drinking bassist's trap door, and about the six-piece band on the Paul English Players show.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: And, uh, it was Charlie Christen on the trombone and, uh, uh, myself, Willie Guitars played bass and lived on Music Street. He used to have a little trap, trap, door, door on the bass, you know, and we'd always wonder because he used to drink, you know, plenty. So, we'd always wonder, say, well, how the devil could he, he'd get drunk that quick? See? So, he'd carry his whiskey and a little medicine bottle, see, and that little trap door in them days in the bass. So, he'd open up the trap door and pull a bottle out and take some more medicine. He said, man, I got a terrible cold tonight. Funchest thing you know, about 10 o'clock, he was riding a bass all over the floor. Man, he was knocked out. I guess that trap door came in. Oh, that trap door, man, was something for him. I'll tell you that right now, man. He really got his kicks in that deal. Having a nice, that's a tense show we're talking about. Oh, yeah. One-nighters. We used to make, that's, that's, uh, Paul English Players. I trooped on that show for about a year.
How big a band would you have in that band?
Oh, we had six men in that band.
Any new orange guys in there besides you? All new orange guys?
No, all the rest of them from Baton Rouge and then, they had a boy from up around Mississippi. I don't know, I was the only one from him. Old Baton Rouge boy.
Yeah, I had a mustache and a, you know, a pair of golf pants on. There was a golf in them days, too. They golfed the liquor, though. What you could get.
